source.title: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains
source.authors: D. Cho; Cameron Tice; Bernie Hogan; Hunar Batra; Puria Radmard; Jun Zhao; Nigel Shadbolt

record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses shallow alignment and fine-tuning fragility, but its own evaluations do not measure any of the listed claim versions. Its blackmail results concern agentic behavior, not refusal or compliance with harmful user requests.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates constitutional midtraining and alignment outcomes after SFT and benign fine-tuning. It does not measure harmful-request refusal rates, per-token KL by response position, compliant-token prefills, suffix or decoding attacks, safety localization in weights, or safety deepening beyond early tokens. Its agentic-blackmail result is recorded under fits_no_version because it is a different behavior from harmful-request compliance.
record.test_reason: The paper cites shallow, fragile post-training alignment as motivation. Its own measurements are agentic blackmail, A/B alignment propensity, alignment faking, emergent misalignment, pressure and value-conflict scores, across midtraining, SFT and benign GRPO stages. It never measures refusal of, or compliance with, harmful user requests by a safety-trained model. It also has no per-token KL, no prefill, suffix or decoding attacks, no weight localization, and no training aimed at deepening safety past the first tokens. The benign GRPO stage resembles V2, but it starts from base-plus-value-neutral-SFT models and the outcomes are different constructs.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that constitutional midtraining gives alignment gains on ID, OOD and blackmail that persist through SFT and benign fine-tuning at no capability cost. Gains on pressure, value conflict and alignment faking attenuate after SFT. Curriculum ordering and deliberative reasoning have only small, transient effects, so content presence matters more than structure.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains constitutional content during midtraining and evaluates after shared SFT and benign GRPO fine-tuning; it does not use the harmful/benign fine-tuning recipes or token-position measurements in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by benchmark and training stage: the blackmail advantage persists through post-BFT, while pressure, value conflict, and alignment-faking advantages attenuate after SFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Pooled CMT models blackmailed less than control at every stage: 0.5% vs 19.0% post-MT, 25.3% vs 44.0% post-SFT, 26.5% vs 44.0% post-BFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Constitutional midtraining reduces agentic blackmail propensity, and the reduction persists through SFT and benign RL fine-tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign GRPO on GSM8K left the control's blackmail rate unchanged (44.0% post-SFT and post-BFT) and OOD alignment essentially unchanged (94.0% to 94.7%). Value-neutral SFT on the base model raised blackmail in every group (control 19% to 44%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign RL fine-tuning on math does not raise agentic misalignment in this setup, whereas generic instruction SFT on a base model increases blackmail propensity.

record.problems: The study uses one hybrid Mamba-attention model and one constitution. The authors note that post-training runs are much smaller than the largest open-source runs, there is no content-matched SFT baseline, and the blackmail evaluation is a forced-dilemma benchmark rather than a deployment-rate estimate. Blackmail classification uses a conservative rule requiring an email, specified keywords, and a judge verdict.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples; no harmful-request compliance rates.
Benign GRPO on GSM8K is applied, but harmful-request refusal or compliance is never measured. The models are not conventionally safety-aligned before BFT (base plus value-neutral SFT).
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL by response position.
No prefilling, adversarial suffixes or decoding manipulations.
No parameter, weight or rank localization or ablation.
Content, ordering and reasoning are varied, but shallowness itself is never measured or explained.
Durability of midtraining effects is tested, but not whether safety extends beyond the opening tokens or survives attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Relation and tranche are confirmed as discusses/T6. The rows correctly carry versions ['none']; their values and baselines match Table 2 and §4.4. The control's unchanged blackmail and OOD scores across BFT are a possible point of contrast with V2-style erosion claims. However, the construct differs (agentic blackmail and A/B propensity, not harmful-request compliance) and the pre-BFT model is not a standard safety-tuned chat model, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a V2 verdict.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or harmful-request refusal/compliance rates.
Benign GRPO fine-tuning is applied, but the paper does not measure refusal of harmful user requests; its blackmail evaluation is agentic behavior.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes.
No weight or rank localization/ablation of safety behavior.
The study varies constitutional content, ordering, and reasoning, but does not test why safety behavior is shallow or measure shallowness.
The study tests durability of constitutional-midtraining effects, not whether training spreads safety beyond the first response tokens.
